## Verdict
REVISE — Explicit lifecycle and identity safeguards are needed before implementation; unavailable hardware may remain an honestly reported gate.

## Critical gaps
- `START_NOT_STICKY` does not prevent recreation while `BIND_AUTO_CREATE` bindings remain. Define stop/unbind, pending-start cancellation, process-death confirmation, and explicit restart authorization so recreation cannot silently resume networking.
- App-private storage alone is insufficient: exclude identity/upstream state from backup and device transfer, and fail closed on corrupt persisted cryptographic state rather than regenerating keys.

## Important improvements
- Promote the service to foreground before potentially slow Python initialization; enable radio operations only after on-device G0 passes.
- Specify B’s accepted-socket association with the correct `Network`, scoped IPv6 endpoint, and discovery session. Outbound socket binding alone cannot establish this. Provision secured-path credentials out of band, without shipped defaults.

## Validation gaps
- Device G0: offline cold startup, actual crypto operations, identity continuity across process replacement, corrupt-state rejection, IPC caller/size rejection, Binder death, and stop/crash/start races with retained bindings.
- Device G1: on every relay configuration, demonstrate concurrent bidirectional A–B/B–C traffic for the design’s 30-minute screen-on/screen-off checks. Record network handles, scoped endpoints, counters, overlap, and disconnects; test wrong credentials and permission/availability loss.
- Host tests and APK assembly cannot establish either device gate. Record unexecuted checks as pending, not passed.

## Recommended revision
1. Resolve and lock the proposed toolchain, Python artifacts, native dependencies, hashes, and distribution obligations.
2. Implement the G0 probe with the lifecycle/storage safeguards above; retain the planned host/build checks.
